$comment: Kiln's install for this frame, as data. Format: docs/design/kiln/frames-as-data.md. A draft (#621): the contract (kiln/apps/kiln/test/contract) reads route, touch and each step's id, writes, reboots, downloads and taps; the engine reads the rest from phase 2. `words`: what Kiln's screens say for this frame (the shared wizard reads them, #621).

releases.why: Glassworks: vX.Y.Z (every release so far) or aqara-s1-plus-vX.Y.Z, and the S1's armeabi-v7a APK

apk.why: The app is the newest S1 release's APK, read when someone installs, so a release reaches Kiln with no deploy. A kiosk-apk staged with Kiln (npm run stage, a local build) still wins, for testing

legacy.why: s1.edm.sh, the first installer page, was the S1's: its hash links (/#/wifi) lead here

enter.why: Stock software has no adb: FEL is the only way in. The button is under the back cover (recovery.json).

time.why: total: the frame's README and docs/install.md (What you need, Before you start), also the picker's What you'll need line. first-boot: docs/install.md, the second Your turn (First boot takes one to two minutes). The FEL boot, backup, patch and write have no timed source yet, so their rows show none

recoverySteps: **Take out the 9 screws** in the back cover.
**Find the recovery button** on the board, right of the metal shield’s notch and below the round sensor window. It’s not the reset button on the case.
**Hold the button and plug in the USB-C cable** from this computer.
**Let go after about 2 seconds.** The screen stays black, which is normal.

drivers.win: Try finding the panel first: click Connect and look for USB Device (1f3a:efe8). If it doesn’t appear (or won’t open), use Zadig to give it the WinUSB driver once, then unplug and reconnect it.
drivers.linux: Try finding the panel first: click Connect and look for USB Device (1f3a:efe8). If it doesn’t appear (or won’t open), add a udev rule once for 1f3a:efe8 and 1f3a:1010, then unplug and reconnect it.

factory.title: As it came from Aqara
factory.detail: Restores the original software, then lets you factory-reset the panel so everything starts fresh.
factory.restored: One last step on the panel: swipe down, tap Settings on the notification, then Advanced settings → Factory reset.

keep.title: Keep its settings
keep.detail: Brings back Aqara's built-in apps while keeping your Wi-Fi and panel settings intact.
keep.stillOn: Aqara's apps are back, though Glassworks is still running
keep.restored: Your panel is restarting with Aqara's original software and apps. Your Wi-Fi and settings stayed intact.

on.line: Updates from Home Assistant install automatically in the background.

missing.line: Each update asks for a tap on the panel. Run Kiln again anytime to enable automatic updates.

unknown.line: Kiln couldn't read this back — check Settings → Device on the panel to see its status.

needs: A USB-C data cable, plugged straight into this computer
A small screwdriver, for the back cover
picker.wayBack: Kiln backs up the panel before it writes anything. Undo puts its original software back.
picker.why: The picker's What you'll need bar (#672), as the frame's README says it (What you need). Its time line comes from words.time.total
